observations.situation: Guest clicked mid-park, Objectives panel also open (pz_guest_info_panel_and_objectives.jpg); Zoo Overview screen open (pz_zoo_overview_panel.jpg)
observations.observation: Contextual side-panels dock to screen edges at roughly 20-35% width; the 3D world keeps rendering at full brightness/animation (guests walking, water moving) in the remaining space in every captured state, including the widest 'Zoo Overview' screen which still leaves the top-right third as a live unobstructed camera view.
observations.designLesson: Never fully obscure the world, even at the heaviest management screen — panels are edge-docked overlays, not modal blackouts.
observations.transfers: A left people-rail / right pictures-rail HUD should dock at fixed screen fractions and always leave the central lot rendering/animating, even when the deepest overview panel is open.
observations.doesNotTransfer: The 3D free-orbiting camera context that motivates this in Planet Zoo doesn't map 1:1 to a fixed isometric 2D camera; the discipline to keep is 'don't cover the lot,' not 'preserve camera freedom.'

observations.situation: Single staff member clicked (pc_frame_staffcard.jpg); full Park Status > Staff tab open (pc_frame_vendorlist.jpg)
observations.observation: Two distinct panel weights exist: a narrow single-entity card (name, one status line, a ring/star rating, 1-2 bars, no wage numbers) versus a wide full-tab screen with a horizontal 9-tab strip (Overview/Finance/Research/Marketing/Staff/Guests/Attractions & Shops/Security/Special Effects) and a sortable numeric table (Name/Workload/Happiness/Training Level/Pay/Roster Assignment).
observations.designLesson: Glanceable per-entity card vs. deliberate numeric decision screen are visually and structurally distinct surfaces, not one panel that expands.
observations.transfers: Build two explicit surfaces: a small click/hover card (status color, 2-3 bars, no raw numbers) and a separate wide 'Studio Overview' reached deliberately for payroll/morale tables with real numbers.
observations.doesNotTransfer: Coaster's 9-tab icon-only horizontal strip is already dense enough that players (see S5) missed tools; don't copy the icon-only tab count as-is — cap lower or label by default.

observations.situation: Keeper clicked in a sandbox tutorial session, ~06:00 in-game elapsed time (pz_frame_360_vet_hire_panel.jpg)
observations.observation: Compact keeper card shows name, 4 icon-only tabs, a one-word status ('Wandering'), a 5-star skill row, two colored need-bars, and an empty 'Recent thoughts' list slot — all within roughly a quarter of the 640px-wide capture, world fully visible and moving behind it.
observations.designLesson: Status is communicated with color/bars/stars, not numbers, at the compact-card tier; numeric wage/percentage detail is reserved for the wide table screen.
observations.transfers: A people-rail card should show a status bar/color, not a raw morale number; keep numeric payroll data in a dedicated table screen only.
observations.doesNotTransfer: n/a — pattern scales down cleanly to 2D with no adaptation needed.

observations.situation: Temperature heatmap active over a mixed hot/cold habitat area (pz_temperature_heatmap.jpg); power heatmap active over a snowy zone (pz_power_heatmap.jpg)
observations.observation: Each heatmap is a full-scene color tint (not a low-opacity permanent layer) triggered from one small top-center rounded panel holding a row of category icons (paw/toilet/thermometer/water-drop/lightning/home/graduation-cap/people) plus a one-line gradient legend for whichever category is active; only one heatmap tints the whole screen at a time, and the bottom toolbar/currency HUD stays unaffected underneath.
observations.designLesson: Heatmaps are an explicit, exclusive full-tint MODE the player toggles into, with the category switcher staying visible so switching between heatmap types doesn't require exiting the mode.
observations.transfers: A studio HUD's problem-spotting overlay (fatigue, foot-traffic) should use the same shape: one persistent small category switcher, a one-line legend, all-or-nothing tint.
observations.doesNotTransfer: Full-scene desaturating tint works against Planet Zoo's highly saturated photoreal 3D; in a flatter 2D isometric style, tinting every asset (including foliage/rockwork) risks crushing the art identity faster — consider tinting only the floor/ground plane instead.

observations.situation: Guest card open, showing per-guest thought log (pz_guest_info_panel_and_objectives.jpg)
observations.observation: A 'RECENT THOUGHTS' section inside the individual guest's own card lists 3 one-line thoughts, each with a small colored face-icon (orange neutral / green happy / red unhappy) and what appears to be a location-jump pin icon; this only appears once that specific guest is clicked, and is not a park-wide ticker or notification feed.
observations.designLesson: Individual-level complaint/mood detail lives inside that entity's own card, keeping the global HUD reading only aggregates (e.g. the separate Zoo Overview screen shows an aggregate 'Guest Happiness 79%' bar, not individual gripes).
observations.transfers: A staff/actor card in a people rail can show 2-3 recent gripe lines the same way, while the main HUD only ever shows an aggregate morale bar.
observations.doesNotTransfer: The location-jump-pin's actual click behavior is inference, not observed being clicked in any video — treat that specific interaction as unverified.

observations.situation: World scenery/animal selected in a mid-build screenshot (pz_ss/pz_17.jpg, pz_ss/pz_18.jpg) plus a no-selection baseline (pz_frame_255_staff_side_panel.jpg)
observations.observation: Selection is shown with a thin flat green ring/ellipse drawn on the ground plane around the selected object plus a dashed yellow rectangle marking its footprint — a diagetic, perspective-following marker rather than a screen-space highlight box; when nothing is selected, staff-facility icons sit in the world with no chrome at all.
observations.designLesson: Selection feedback is drawn into the 3D world itself (ground-plane decal) rather than as UI chrome, keeping it visually integrated with photoreal art instead of feeling like an overlay.
observations.transfers: A 2D isometric lot can use a flat ground-plane highlight (an outlined isometric tile/diamond) under a selected desk/prop for the same 'belongs to the world' feel.
observations.doesNotTransfer: The literal circular-ellipse shape is a 3D-perspective artifact; the isometric equivalent is a diamond/tile outline, not a circle. Also: hover-vs-click distinction for this marker was NOT observed in any video sequence — not-verified whether hover alone shows a lighter version.

observations.situation: Steam Community thread, Planet Zoo, opened launch week
observations.observation: Original poster (Nov 14, 2019) listed concrete friction points including 'Building barriers click by agonising click. Can't I just drag?' and lack of error feedback for failed placements; replier AngryWolf agreed the interface 'is not an intuitive interface at all' and called camera controls 'really wonky,' while other repliers (DementedGnome, Nariel) pointed out that a lasso multi-select tool already existed but had gone unnoticed by the OP.
observations.designLesson: A meaningful share of launch-week UI frustration was about discoverability of existing tools/gestures, not their total absence — icon-only or non-obvious controls cost real player time even when the feature exists.
observations.transfers: Don't assume an included feature solves a UX complaint just because it exists — verify it's discoverable (tooltip-on-first-hover, in-context hint) before shipping.
observations.doesNotTransfer: The specific camera-control complaints are Planet Zoo's own control-scheme choices, not directly relevant to a 2D isometric HUD's camera needs.

observations.situation: Steam Community thread, Planet Zoo, opened launch week, still unresolved per a quoted 2025 follow-up
observations.observation: Original poster (Sep 24, 2019), self-identified as visually impaired: 'I am very visually impaired and the surfaces and texts in the game are too small.' A moderator (HeatherG) confirmed scaling up to 160% cuts off menu edges, with the only in-game steps jumping straight from 100% to 160% (no middle ground); the practical workaround players adopted was hand-editing Game_local.config.xml to intermediate values like 1.2 (120%). A user (TheScaredMarine) asked in July 2025 whether the issue was ever fixed, implying it persisted for over 5 years without an official granular fix.
observations.designLesson: Shipping only two coarse UI-scale steps left a real accessibility gap for years; players had to resort to config-file edits for anything in between.
observations.transfers: Ship a continuous UI-scale slider from the outset rather than 2-3 discrete steps, and test the smallest supported text size against the densest simultaneous panel state before launch.
observations.doesNotTransfer: The specific 100%/160% values are Planet Zoo's own implementation detail, cited only as an example of insufficient granularity, not a target to imitate.

observations.situation: Park Status > Staff tab open with a vendor list, live booth-camera thumbnail visible at panel edge (pc_frame_vendorlist.jpg)
observations.observation: Even the widest captured management screen keeps a small secondary live-rendered viewport into the world (the booth interior the selected vendor works in) rather than replacing the world entirely with a stat block; this mirrors the Zoo Overview screen's preserved live camera strip (Observation 1).
observations.designLesson: Even the deepest management view treats 'keep some view of the world visible' as non-negotiable, reinforcing that the player is managing their park/zoo, not reading an abstracted spreadsheet.
observations.transfers: A studio HUD's fullest 'Studio Overview' screen should likewise preserve a visible strip of the actual lot.
observations.doesNotTransfer: Compositing a second live camera viewport (as Coaster does for the booth) is a heavier real-time rendering cost; a 2D engine gets the same effect more cheaply by simply never covering the single main view, rather than adding a second rendered camera.

observations.situation: Zoo Overview screen's left vertical icon rail (pz_zoo_overview_panel.jpg); compact keeper card's 4-icon tab row (pz_frame_360_vet_hire_panel.jpg)
observations.observation: Tab rails in both the wide and compact panels use icon-only glyphs (clipboard/coin/paw/staff/ranger-hat/wrench/house on the wide screen; 4 unlabeled icons on the compact card) with no visible text labels in any captured state.
observations.designLesson: Both games bet on genre-standard pictograms (paw, coin, wrench) to save space; the bet mostly pays off for very standard concepts but the S5 thread shows the same icon-only philosophy elsewhere in the UI cost some players real discoverability.
observations.transfers: Use icon-only tabs for universally standard concepts (dollar sign for finance, person for HR) but pair less-standard icons with a first-hover tooltip or persistent label at smaller HUD densities.
observations.doesNotTransfer: Don't treat 'icon-only is fine' as a blanket rule — a project-studio HUD's department/project-type icon vocabulary is far less standardized than zoo/coaster genre icons and more likely to need labels.

unverified: Hover-vs-click distinction for the ground-plane selection marker (Observation/frame pz_ss/pz_18.jpg) — only a static selected-state still was found; no video sequence showed the hover state or the click transition.
Exact right-click and keyboard-shortcut behavior in either game — no viewed source showed a keybind overlay or right-click context menu.
Whether Planet Coaster's reported 4K auto-70%-scale figure (S7) is still accurate or was later patched — only a WebSearch snippet summary was obtained, not the primary thread text.

The 7-category welfare breakdown (Nutrition/Hydration/Social/Space/Stress/Habitat/Enrichment) often cited for Planet Zoo's Animal Information Panel — the wiki page (S8) returned HTTP 402 and was never directly viewed; this list is not included as a numbered observation because of that.
The location-jump-pin icon's click behavior in the guest 'Recent thoughts' list — inferred from icon appearance only, not observed being activated.

comp:planet.summary: Gathered strong primary visual evidence for both original titles (Planet Coaster 2016, Planet Zoo 2019 — explicitly NOT Planet Coaster 2 or the Console Edition) via 43 official Steam screenshots and two dated, identifiable YouTube gameplay/tutorial videos (frames extracted, videos deleted after). Found and directly quoted two dated Steam Community threads on reported UI frustrations (icon/gesture discoverability at Planet Zoo's Nov 2019 launch; a persistent, still-unresolved-as-of-2025 UI-scaling/accessibility gap from Sep 2019). Produced 10 concrete, evidence-cited observations covering: never-obscured world behind panels, two-tier panel weight (compact card vs. full tab screen), bar/star/ring status language on compact cards, full-tint exclusive heatmap mode with persistent category switcher, per-entity 'recent thoughts' logs vs. aggregate HUD stats, diagetic ground-plane selection markers, reported discoverability/scaling complaints (directly quoted), preserved live-world viewport even in the widest management screen, and icon-only tab rails as a discoverability risk. Two sources were blocked (Fandom wiki HTTP 402, MobyGames HTTP 403) and are flagged; a handful of specific behaviors (hover-state selection, keybinds, one search-summary-only 4K stat, and the wiki's 7-category welfare list) are explicitly marked unverified rather than asserted.

observations.situation: 5 official RCT2 marketing screenshots (rct2_steam_1..5.jpg), no window open in any
observations.observation: RCT2's entire persistent chrome is two small icon clusters (top-left ~6 icons: new/save/zoom/map/scenario-info; top-right ~8 icons: build categories) plus a single-line bottom status bar (cash + guest count left, one center message-ticker slot e.g. "Twist 1 has broken down"/"Big Wheel has broken down", date/weather/rating right). Chrome occupies well under 10% of vertical screen space; the isometric park is fully visible at all times.
observations.transfers: A studio-management HUD can keep always-on chrome to two edge clusters (left people-rail toggle, right pictures-rail toggle) plus one persistent bottom status line, leaving the lot dominant.
observations.doesNotTransfer: RCT2's icons are cryptic single-glyph buttons with no text, ~20-24px, fine for a 2002 series-trained audience but risky for a new IP without tooltips/onboarding.
observations.designLesson: Persistent chrome budget can be intentionally tiny and symmetric; everything else is negotiated on demand via small pop-up windows rather than permanently reserved screen area.

observations.situation: "New Gentle Rides" build-selection window open over an active park, frame at ~3:36 in source video
observations.observation: The ride picker is a small (~330x230px at 640x360 capture) draggable red-bordered window: title bar + close box, a 5x2 grid of ~48px picture-tile icons (tiny isometric renders of each ride type), and below the grid a single enlarged preview of the selected tile plus one line of flavor text and one line of stats ("2 designs available, no vehicles displayed/hidden layout"). The built park stays visible and unblurred around the window.
observations.transfers: Validates a right "pictures rail" pattern: a grid of picture-tile thumbnails with one expanded detail card, kept as a floating/anchored panel rather than a full-screen gallery that hides the lot.
observations.doesNotTransfer: This is a transient window the player explicitly opens and closes per purchase, not a permanently-docked rail; don't cite RCT2 as evidence for constant-visibility furniture if the target HUD wants an always-open rail.
observations.designLesson: Browsing a catalog of buildable things does not require leaving the world or covering the screen.

observations.situation: Selected guest and a ride-in-progress in two different marketing screenshots
observations.observation: A small black-outlined white-text label ("Dianna S. (Walking)" in rct2_steam_3.jpg; "Guest: X people in ride" in rct2_f112.jpg/rct2_f216.jpg) is drawn directly in the world next to the relevant sprite -- not inside any window chrome -- and appears only for the current selection.
observations.transfers: A central lot can show a lightweight in-world nameplate/status chip over a selected staffer or in-progress project marker without needing a rail expanded.
observations.doesNotTransfer: RCT2 only ever shows one such label at a time (current selection); not license for permanent multi-label clutter across the whole lot.
observations.designLesson: Cheap at-a-glance identification can live in the world itself instead of requiring an opened window, preserving peripheral awareness without stealing screen space.

observations.situation: Manual's own build-a-ride tutorial (pp.12-14) walks through the Ride window's 5 tabs while other tasks continue
observations.observation: The manual has the player open a Ride window, switch among View/Measurements/Income&Costs/Operation Options tabs to finish configuring one ride, then move on while leaving windows open; the RCT2 gameplay contact sheet (rct2_sheet.jpg) confirms 2-4 small red-bordered windows open and overlapping simultaneously at multiple points in the recording (e.g., near 1:50-2:00).
observations.transfers: Small floating cards (a staff card + a project card, etc.) can legitimately coexist over a visible world -- the 'toolbox of small non-modal windows' pattern is worth keeping.
observations.doesNotTransfer: RCT2 shows no window-count management -- no tray, no 'recently closed', no cap; a modern HUD should add bookkeeping RCT2 lacks rather than copy unmanaged window sprawl (see also the RCT3 juggling complaints below).
observations.designLesson: RCT2's management model is an explicit toolbox of small non-modal windows the player leaves open and returns to, not a single dialog flow.

observations.situation: Bottom status bar center slot across 3 different marketing screenshots, including one German-localized build
observations.observation: The identical UI slot (bottom-center of the status bar) carries exactly one line of highlighted alert text naming the single most urgent event -- "Twist 1 has broken down" (English), "Piratenschiff 1 ist ausgefallen" (German, same slot, different length), "Big Wheel has broken down" (English) -- with no badge count or stacked toast list visible in any shot.
observations.transfers: A bottom status strip with one rotating most-urgent-alert line is a low-cost, localization-robust pattern (English and German text of very different length both fit because the field takes one flexible line, not a fixed pixel width per word).
observations.doesNotTransfer: Single-slot design has no visible mechanism for surfacing a second simultaneous urgent event; a HUD needing to report multiple concurrent alerts (e.g., two blocked projects) must go beyond this pattern.
observations.designLesson: One unambiguous 'most important thing right now' text slot is legible at a glance and localization-safe.

observations.situation: 6 RCT3 Complete Edition gameplay frames from a near-top-down camera (rct3_f40/150/210/270/330/420.jpg)
observations.observation: RCT3 replaces RCT2's two-corner clusters with a single vertical stack of ~8 small (~28px) circular icon buttons down the far-left edge, plus a thin dark horizontal strip across the very top (save/load/speed/chat icons) and a small circular minimap in the bottom-left corner.
observations.transfers: An edge-anchored rail (vs. floating corner clusters) reads as more 'toolbox' and maps directly onto a left people-rail concept -- RCT3 validates a permanent left-edge icon rail coexisting with a fully-visible 3D lot behind it.
observations.doesNotTransfer: RCT3's rail icons are undifferentiated small circles requiring memorization/hover, the same legibility limitation as RCT2 -- not a model to copy for icon clarity.
observations.designLesson: Moving chrome from two top corners to one full edge frees the top of the screen (useful with a free 3D camera that often looks toward the horizon) but costs horizontal width on widescreen monitors regardless of aspect ratio.

observations.situation: Scenery/path tool active (rct3_f270.jpg, rct3_f420.jpg) and various ride selections under cursor (rct3_f150/210/270/420.jpg)
observations.observation: A narrow vertical build-list panel anchors directly to the right of the icon rail when a tool is active, showing 3-4 rows of thumbnail+name+price ("Path edge (corner) $10", "Atlantis Bench $3", "Atlantis Bin $3", "Atlantis Clam Shell Lamp $2"). Independently, a small semi-transparent dark-blue card near the bottom-right shows a 3-line live inspector for the hovered/selected ride (name, "Capacity: N passengers per car", "Cars per train" with an increment control), updating as the cursor moves between rides ("Splash Boats", "Storm Runner Car", "Coasterball Car" all observed in different frames).
observations.transfers: The anchored-list-next-to-rail is a strong candidate for a pictures rail (thumbnails+name+one stat, no separate window chrome to browse); the live-follows-selection inspector card is a strong pattern for at-a-glance stats on whatever is selected in the lot, without a modal.

comp:rct.summary: Gathered primary evidence for RCT2 (2002, current Steam Triple Thrill Pack build) and RCT3 (2004 engine, current Steam Complete Edition) covering: RCT2's minimal two-corner-cluster + single status-bar chrome model with fully visible isometric world at all times (5 official Steam screenshots, zero windows open); a concrete captured frame of RCT2's compact icon-grid ride-picker window with live preview pane; in-world floating name/status labels substituting for opened windows; the manual-documented and video-confirmed 'toolbox of small non-modal windows' juggling pattern (2-4 windows open at once); and the single-slot bottom-center alert ticker. For RCT3, captured 9 gameplay frames showing a single vertical left-edge icon rail (replacing RCT2's two clusters), an anchored build-list panel next to the rail, and a small live-updating inspector card that follows the hovered/selected ride -- plus the finding that RCT3's own marketing screenshots (6/6) show zero UI, a deliberate spectacle-first identity choice distinct from RCT2's toolbar-is-the-identity marketing. Community evidence (two dated, quoted Steam Community threads) documents a reported 'worst interface' opinion (contested within its own thread) and a concrete, unresolved 4K UI-scaling failure in RCT3 Platinum. All observations are tied to viewed screenshots/manual pages/video frames and cite exact source and, where applicable, timestamp/frame file.</summary>
